answer: Each agent earns spending credit only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result another agent can verify against a hidden test; a deposit is forfeited when the result fails. This makes identity count alone worthless: a sybil farm must solve many tasks and lock capital for each attempt, while honest agents can reuse reputation instead of paying again. A plume of fresh accounts cannot cheaply wind through the vine of checks, and the dune of required deposits raises the attacker's cost with every identity.
